input: Research local foster care volunteering requirements

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Foster care volunteering covers very different roles — tutoring, respite care, mentoring, administrative support, etc. The requirements vary drastically by role, so knowing which type narrows the research significantly.
Requirements are set at the state or county level and differ widely by location. Knowing the specific city, county, or state determines which agencies and regulations are actually relevant.
Whether the user is researching for themselves alone, as a couple, or as a family affects which requirements apply (e.g., household background checks, home assessments).
The user may have a hard limit on time per week or a specific availability window, which would filter out roles with intensive hour requirements or mandatory training schedules.
Some people want direct, hands-on contact with children; others prefer support roles. This shapes which agencies or programs to prioritize in the research.
The user may want a simple overview to decide if volunteering is feasible, or a detailed step-by-step action plan to actually apply. The depth of research needed differs entirely.
Knowing whether the user wants a compiled written summary, a list of links/contacts, or is ready to make calls/visits determines the immediate next action and output format.

gold.taskTitle: Research local foster care volunteering requirements
gold.taskDescription: Find out what is required to volunteer with a local foster care organization or agency.

questions.title: What type of volunteer role interests you most?
questions.description: Identify the specific volunteer role the user is considering, such as mentoring, respite care, tutoring, transportation, or administrative support, since requirements differ significantly by role.

questions.title: Which city or county are you researching this for?
questions.description: Pinpoint the user's location at the city or county level, as foster care volunteer requirements are governed locally and vary widely by jurisdiction.

questions.title: Are you researching this for yourself or your whole household?
questions.description: Determine whether the research covers one individual or multiple household members, since some roles require background checks or assessments for everyone in the home.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you realistically commit?
questions.description: Establish the user's available time so that roles with intensive hour or training requirements that exceed their capacity can be filtered out early.

questions.title: Do you want direct contact with children or a support role?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prefers working directly with foster children or supporting the system in a behind-the-scenes capacity, which shapes which programs to focus on.

questions.title: Do you want a quick overview or a detailed application roadmap?
questions.description: Determine the depth of research needed — whether the user wants a high-level feasibility check or a thorough step-by-step guide to actually applying as a volunteer.

questions.title: What format should the final research output take?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants a written summary, a list of agency contacts and links, a checklist, or another format so the output matches how they plan to use it.
